proof.label: Sample

reviews.text: My dad started this shop and I always figured my daughter would get it someday. Marcus made us put a year on it, and a list of what she had to learn first. She runs quoting now, and I am down to four days a week.
reviews.name: Gary H.

reviews.text: He walked the floor with me on a Tuesday morning and pointed out that every job waited at the same saw. We moved one person and changed the order we cut in.
reviews.name: Rhonda P.

reviews.text: I was not ready to sell and said so. We spent the first months just getting the numbers clean and the jobs written down, which is worth doing either way.
reviews.name: Dennis J.

reviews.text: Two of our biggest customers pay on sixty days and the steel bill comes in thirty. The cash calendar finally put that on one page where my wife and I could both see it.
reviews.name: Luis M.

reviews.text: I had coaching sessions, and separately so did my shop lead, who is buying in over five years. Hearing the same plan from both sides kept us from talking past each other.
reviews.name: Annette B.

reviews.text: Job costing showed the small rush orders we loved were paying for nothing. We kept them but priced them like rush work. Simple, once somebody laid it out.
reviews.name: Wendell F.

proof.guarantee: Stop after any month with no penalty, and keep everything we wrote together.

prices.note: half-day on site plus written notes
